description: The bar chart illustrates the difference in average Word Error Rate (WER) from Whisper large for various optimisations applied to two models: the NESAC ft model (brown bars) and the SESHA ft model (green bars). The horizontal axis represents the "Difference in Average WER from Whisper large" on a linear scale ranging from 0.000 to 0.004, while the vertical axis lists the optimisations applied: "Dates," "Americanisms," "Remove Spacing," "Add Spacing," and "Normalised." For each optimisation, the chart compares the performance of the two models. The NESAC ft model consistently shows a higher WER difference than the SESHA ft model across all five optimisations. The highest WER difference is observed for the "Add Spacing" optimisation, with the NESAC ft model at 0.00319 and the SESHA ft model at 0.00344. The lowest WER difference is for the "Dates" optimisation, with the NESAC ft model at 0.00257 and the SESHA ft model at 0.00228. The data indicates that the SESHA ft model generally performs better (i.e., has a lower WER difference) than the NESAC ft model under the tested optimisations.
